exact_reviewed_text.pl_statement: According to PFRON (26 October 2026), the Polish Accessibility Act does not impose a general requirement for a separate website accessibility statement. Covered service providers must publish accessible information about their service, its use and how it meets accessibility requirements in terms and conditions or an equivalent document.
exact_reviewed_text.pl_reporting: PFRON states that Article 67 notifications have no specified deadline after discovery. Separate duties require manufacturers and service providers to notify the competent authority without delay in the circumstances of Articles 27(2) and 32(2)(6).
exact_reviewed_text.pl_activity: In its reply of 26 October 2026, PFRON confirmed that it had begun monitoring accessibility compliance. Depending on the findings, inspections and administrative decisions may follow. The reply did not confirm whether any measures had been taken or any outcomes reached.
exact_reviewed_text.pl_extra: Optional dark mode can be assessed. Information about operators being monitored may be disclosed under the Access to Public Information Act. Each disclosure must be assessed individually and is subject to legal restrictions, including protection of business secrets.
exact_reviewed_text.be_statement: For consumer banking and e-commerce, Economic Inspection confirms that information assessing how the service meets the accessibility requirements must be published in the terms and conditions or an equivalent document, and made publicly available in written and oral formats accessible to persons with disabilities.
exact_reviewed_text.be_activity: Economic Inspection’s reply of 19 December 2025 covered only its responsibilities for consumer banking and e-commerce. It reported that it had received consumer complaints and launched investigations since 28 June 2025.
exact_reviewed_text.be_limits: The supplied replies did not confirm the number of complaints or investigations, whether any warnings or penalties had been issued, or any outcomes.

Poland

According to PFRON (26 October 2026), the Polish Accessibility Act does not impose a general requirement for a separate website accessibility statement. Covered service providers must publish accessible information about their service, its use and how it meets accessibility requirements in terms and conditions or an equivalent document.

Official authority correspondence (research record).

E-commerce:

  • Minister of Digital Affairs — e-commerce services.

Banking:

  • Financial Ombudsman — retail banking services.
